newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares hit record on rate cut hopes.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares hit record on rate cut hopes.

text.p: Israeli shares rose to a record high on Sunday on expectations the central bank will cut interest rates on Monday, traders said.

The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 0.77 percent, or 2.06 points, to 271.06 on all-share turnover of 130 million shekels against 158 million shekels on Thursday, the last day of trading before the Israeli weekend.
The previous high was reached on February 18, when the Mishtanim hit 270.87.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.57 percent higher at 279.35.

"The market is very strong and it continues to rise. The main reason for today's gain is the fact that the market expects a rate cut of 0.3 to 0.5 percentage point," said Amir Eyal at Epsilon Securities.
The Bank of Israel will publish its key lending rate for June on May 26. The central bank last cut its base rate to 13.9 percent at the end of February.

"Everybody expects a rate cut of as much as 0.5 point. If the central bank decides to leave the rates unchanged it will have a negative impact on trading and the market will start falling," said Yoram Ben-Yair at Ahrayut Investment Management.
"Right now the market looks very good and traders are very optimistic. Activity is rising and the positive trend is clear," Ben-Yair said.

Eyal added that the market was also affected by the continued recovery of the primary market and rising foreign investor interest. "I think that we are at the beginning of a long positive cycle," he said.
Shekem rose 4.5 percent to 120.5 agorot, despite reporting on Sunday that net income in the first quarter of 1997 fell to 1.04 million shekels from 25.4 million a year earlier.

Shekem's parent company Elco Holdings surged 8.5 percent to 2,879 agorot. Elco reported on Sunday that net income in the first quarter fell to 9.4 million shekels from 28.8 million at the same quarter last year.
Traders said that Elco's results were above expectations and that the share's rise was a technical correction after it suffered heavy losses.
Clal Trading closed unchanged at 1,237 agorot. Clal on Sunday reported a first quarter net loss of 16.2 million shekels against net profit of 8.7 million shekels in the same period in 1996.

The most active shares were Israel Discount Bank, which gained 1.25 percent to 371 agorot on volume of 5.9 million shekels; Bezeq Israel Telecom, which rose 3.25 percent to 932 agorot on turnover of 5.5 million shekels; and Azorim Investment Development & Construction, which gained 2.5 percent to 4,022 on volume of 5.3 million shekels.
